matchRule: casefold and remove every character outside [a-z0-9], then require exactly one ontology label (or alias) to normalize to the same key
notes: The audited GNN vocabulary declares `obo:ACTO_*` and `obo:TEMP_*` uri values. Those prefixes do not resolve (no ACTO ontology exists in the OBO Foundry, Bioregistry, or OLS) and are never used as mapping targets; this document maps labels to stable `term-*` IDs only.
`declared` entries with status `unresolved` have no counterpart in the current ontology release; they require ontology curation or GNN-side model migration and are never guessed.

Accuracy.description: Broad sense: how “close to the mark” an Estimator is.

Action.description: Broad sense: The dynamics, mechanisms, and measurements of Behavior

Action Planning.description: The selection of an Affordance based upon Inference of Expected Free Energy

Action Prediction.description: Inference on current and future Expectation of Action

Active Inference.description: Active Inference is a Process Theory related to Free Energy Principle .

Active States.description: In the Friston Blanket formalism, the Blanket State are the Sense State (incoming Sensory input) and Active States (outgoing influence of Policy selection )

Active Vision.description: refers to the process of visual perceptions, in terms of oculomotor Sensorimotor Behavior and Cognitive System Generative Model

Affordance.description: Options or capacities for Action by an Agent (sometimes called “Affordance 3.0”)

Agency.description: The ability of an Agent to engage in Action in their Niche and enact Goal-driven selection or Policy selection based upon Preference

Agent.description: Entity as modeled by Active Inference , with Internal State separated from External State by Blanket State

Ambiguity.description: Broad sense: Extent to which stimuli have multiple plausible interpretations, requiring priors &/or Action for disambiguation

Attention.description: Broad sense: Generative Model that is aware of some Stimulus, reflected by its Salience

Autopoiesis.description: Phenomena of a System that recapitulates the material and informational causes of its own composition/existence.

Bayesian Inference.description: As opposed to frequentist analysis, Bayesian Inference uses a specified Prior or Empirical prior to Update the distributional Posterior

Behavior.description: The sequence of Action that an Agent is observed to enact.

Belief.description: Broad sense: Felt sense by an Agent of something being true, or confidence it is the case.

Belief updating.description: Belief updating is changes in a Bayesian Inference Belief through time.

Blanket State.description: Set of states in the Markov Blanket Partition that make Internal State and External State have Conditional Probability that are independent.

Cognition.description: An Agent modifying the weights of its Internal State for the purpose of Action Planning and/or Belief updating . (This is a @realistCounterpart of Goal-driven selection .)

Complexity.description: The extent to which an Agent must revise a Belief to explain incoming Sensory observations.

Cue.description: a Stimulus , event, object , or Guidance signal that serves to guide Behavior , such as a retrieval cue, or that acts as a @Signal to the presentation of another stimulus, event, or object, such as an unconditioned stimulus or reinforcement. (dictionary.apa.org)

Culture.description: Culture is the Niche for social Agent, that structures their Regime of Attention

Data.description: Data are a set of values of qualitative or quantitative variables about one or more Agent or object .

Decision-making.description: Within Active Inference , this is the same as Policy selection

Ensemble.description: Group of more than one Agent.

Epistemic value.description: is the value of Information gain or Expectation of reduction in Uncertainty about a State with respect to a Policy, used in Policy selection

Evidence.description: Data as recognized and interpreted by Generative Model of Agent

Expectation.description: Within a Bayesian Inference framework, Expectation is an Estimator about future timesteps

Expected Free Energy.description: Measure for performing Inference on Action over a given time horizon (Policy selection , Action and Planning as Divergence Minimization ).

External State.description: States with Conditional density independent from Internal State, conditioned on Blanket State.

Free Energy.description: Free Energy is an Information Theoretic quantity that constitutes an upper bound on Surprisal .

Free Energy Principle.description: A generalization of Predictive Coding (PC) according to which organisms minimize an upper bound on the Entropy of Sensory input (or sensory signals) (the Free Energy). Under specific assumptions, Free Energy translates toPrediction error .

Friston Blanket.description: Markov Blanket with partitioned Active States and Sense State .

Generalized Free Energy.description: Past Variational Free Energy plus future Expected Free Energy (each totaled over Policy).

Generative Model.description: A formalism that describes the mapping between Hidden State, and Expectations of Action Prediction , Sensory outcome .

Generative Process.description: Underlying @dynamical process in the Niche giving rise to Agent Observation and @agent Action Prediction

Hidden State.description: Unobserved variable in Bayesian Inference , can reflect a Latent cause .

Hierarchical Model.description: A hierarchy of Estimators, which operate at different spatiotemporal timescales (so they track features at different scales); all carrying out Predictive Processing

High road.description: One of two roads (arguments) that lead to the Free Energy Principle as a possible conclusion which starts with philosophical questions about what properties a thing must have to “exist” (i.e. it must be measurable) and then uses principles of Autopoiesis and non-equilibrium Thermodynamic systems from a statistical perspective to show what kinds of systems could continue to maintain themselves over time (see Friston 2019: Beyond the Desert Landscape and the other road, the Low road ). “The high road stands in for a top-down approach that starts by asking fundamental questions about the necessary properties things must possess if they exist. Using mathematical (variational) principles, once can then show that existence is an embodied exchange of a creatures with its environment - that necessarily entails predictive processing as one aspect of self-evidencing mechanics.”

Inference.description: Process of reaching a (local or global) conclusion within a Model, for example with Bayesian Inference.

Information.description: Measured in bits, the reduction of Uncertainty on a Belief distribution of some type. Usually Syntactic (Shannon) but also can be Semantic (e.g. Bayesian ).

Information Geometry.description: A Statistical manifold each of whose points corresponds to a Probability distribution (e.g. the expectation and variance of a normal density).

Internal State.description: States with Conditional density independent from External State , conditioned on Blanket State.

Learning.description: Broad sense: Process of an Agent engaged in Updates to Cognition (and possibly) Behavior.

Low road.description: One of two roads (arguments) that lead to the Free Energy Principle as a possible conclusion which starts with fundamental questions from neuroscience and psychology about the nature of perception in biological organisms within a changing environment (see Friston 2019: Beyond the Desert Landscape and the other road, the High road ). “The low road is to pursue the agenda established by Kant and Helmholtz to generalize - in a bottom up way - the capacity for inference and prediction to see how far it takes us in understand embodied exchange with the environment.”

Markov Blanket.description: Markov Partitioning Model of System, reflecting Agent as delineated from the Niche via an Interface. The Markov Blanket Blanket State reflect the State(s) upon which Internal State and External State are conditionally independent.

Markov Decision Process.description: Bayesian Inference Model where Agent Generative Model can implement Policy selection on Affordances reflected by Active States, while other features of the Generative Process are outside the Control (states) of the Agent .

Narrative.description: Information used by Agent in context of entity- and event-oriented Cognition, specifically Hierarchical Model (Hierarchically Mechanistic Mind ).

Niche.description: Ecology System constituting the Generative Process (as Partitioned from the Agent who instantiates a Generative Model ).

Non-Equilibrium Steady State.description: Technically, a Non-Equilibrium Steady State requires a solution to the Fokker Planck equation (i.e., density dynamics). A nonequilibrium steady-state solution entails solenoidal (i.e., conservative or divergence free) dynamics that break detailed balance (and underwrite stochastic chaos ). In other words, The dynamics of systems at Non-Equilibrium Steady State are not time reversible (unlike equilibrium steady states, in which the flow is entirely dissipative).

Novelty.description: The Internal State assumed by an Agent‘s epistemic Affordance, when unable to immediately (e.g. locally) resolve Uncertainty about the contingencies — i.e. the opportunity to resolve Uncertainty about ‘what would happen if I did that?’ (The Precision of this assumed Internal State has a distinctive, e.g. multimodal, distribution, i.e. exhibits Ambiguity .)

Observation.description: The Belief updating of an Internal State registered by a Sensory input, given the weighting assigned to that class of input in comparison with weighting of the competing Priors. (This is a narrow sense of “observation,” where the Agent is “looking for this kind of input.” This sense excludes situations where (a) an incoming stimulus with these attributes has already been explained-away or pre-discounted, or (b) the prior is so strongly weighted as to exclude updating in response to any inputs (other than, perhaps, “catastrophic” ones, as may occur in e.g. fainting, hysterical blindness).)

Outcome.description: If we consider the environment as a Generative Process that can be sampled when in a particular state, the statistical result (Data, Sensory observation) of the sampling is known as the outcome.

Particle.description: An Agent consisting of Blanket State and Internal State , partitioned off from Niche .

Perception.description: Posterior State Inference after each new Observation.

Policy.description: Sequence of Actions, reflected by series of Active States as implemented in Policy selection which is Action Prediction or Action and Planning as Divergence Minimization

Policy selection.description: The process of an Agent engaging in Action Planning from set of Affordance, in Active Inference based upon minimization of Expected Free Energy

Posterior.description: The Update to the Prior after Observation has occurred

Pragmatic Value.description: Pragmatic Value is the benefit to an organism of a given Policy or Action , measured in terms of probability of a Policy leading to Expectation of Random variable values that are aligned with the Preference of the Agent

Prediction.description: An Estimator about a State in a Model at a future time.

Preference.description: parameter in Bayesian Inference Markov Decision Process that ranks or scores the extent to how an Agent values Sensory input .

Prior.description: The initial or preceding state of a Belief in Bayesian Inference, before Sensory Data (Observation or Evidence ) occurs.

Process Theory.description: A hypothesis or Model proposal for how a Principle is realized (e.g. the Free Energy Principle)

Recognition Model.description: Recognition Model is the kind of Model that affords Variational Inference, which lets us calculate or approximate a probability distribution. Recognition Model is a synonym for Variational Model.

Regime of Attention.description: feedback mechanisms among practices in a Culture of scaffolding individuals’ Attention, that guide Agents’ style of Attention; act as determined by bodily, language, and contextual Cues in a given community; and are encoded in higher levels of the cortical hierarchy.

Representation.description: A structural correspondence between some Random variable inside a System and some Random variable outside the System (isomorphism being the strongest kind of correspondence), such that the Systemengages in Inference carried out by the System maintains the correspondence

Salience.description: The extent to which a Cue commands the Attention of an Agent given their Regime of Attention

Sense State.description: In the Friston Blanket formalism, the Blanket State are the Sense State (incoming Sensory input) and Active States (outgoing influence of Policy selection )

Sentience.description: being ‘‘responsive to sensory impressions’’ through adaptive internal processes

State.description: is the statistical, computational, or mathematical value for a parameter within the State space of a Model .

State space.description: Set of variables/parameters that describe a System .

Stationarity.description: Of a Random variable , that it is described by parameters that are drawn from a Gaussian distribution and unchanging over the time horizon of analysis.

Surprise.description: In Bayesian Inference, Surprise is the negative log evidence, directly corresponding to the inverse of probability (high probability, low surprisal; low probability, high surprisal). The proxy that bounds surprisal is the difference between Prior and Posterior Distribution — how “surprising” Sensory Data are to the Generative Model of the Agent.

System.description: Set of relations described by State space of a Model .

Temporal Depth.description: The length of a time window or horizon considered (longer time → deeper / more Temporal Depth )

Uncertainty.description: In Bayesian Inference , a measure of the Expectation of Surprise (Entropy) of a Random variable (associated with its variance or inverse Precision )

Variational.description: Biologically: Said of the behavior of a Neuronal Ensemble that minimizes the error of quantities selected by that ensemble, by implementing an algorithm that approximates calculus of variations.

Variational Free Energy.description: Measure that performs e.g. Inference on Sensory Data given a Generative Model , F. The two sources that composeVariational Free Energy are Model overfitting and Model accuracy

abstractCounterpart.description: (abstractCounterpart ?AB ?PHYS) relates a Physical entity to an Abstract one which is an idealized model in some dimension of the Physical entity.

represents.description: SUMO relation (represents ?THING ?ENTITY) means that ?THING in some way indicates, expresses, connotes, pictures, describes, etc. ?ENTITY. The Predicates containsInformation and realization are subrelations of represents.
